title: Closed support and arbitrary pullback of a finite type module on an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], of finite type, meaning etale locally generated by finitely many sections. Define $\operatorname{Supp}_X(M)=\{x\in|X|:M_{\bar x}\ne0\}$ using geometric stalks, independently of the choice of geometric representative as in [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support], and the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Then $\operatorname{Supp}_X(M)$ is closed. For every morphism $g:Y\to X$ of algebraic spaces over $S$, tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors] gives a finite type quasi-coherent module $g^*M$ and $\operatorname{Supp}_Y(g^*M)=|g|^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}_X(M))$. No flatness, separation, finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $g$ or the spaces.

proof.text: Let $e:U\to X$ be any etale scheme chart. Etale pullback is restriction by [def-trf-algebraic-space], so $e^*M$ remains quasi-coherent and of finite type: restrict the local presentations and the finite generating families. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], write $e^*M\simeq(N_U)_{\mathrm{et}}$ for a quasi-coherent Zariski module $N_U$ on $U$. The finite-type equivalence in [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] implies that $N_U$ is of finite type in the Zariski sense. This does not use a Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: section-properties-modules, etale restriction and comparison with Zariski properties; descent.tex Tags 03DX (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent), 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type](1), $\operatorname{Supp}_U(N_U)$ is closed. By [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support], it equals $|e|^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}_X(M))$. This holds for every etale scheme chart $e$. By [def-a1-space-point-topology], a subset of $|X|$ is closed precisely when its inverse images under all such charts are closed: apply its open-set criterion to the complement. Thus $\operatorname{Supp}_X(M)$ is closed.

source.place: Tag 07TZ (lemma-support-finite-type), proof of (1), using Tag 07TY (lemma-support-covering) and morphisms.tex Tag 056J (lemma-support-finite-type).

proof.text: Fix $g:Y\to X$. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $e:U\to X$ by [def-trf-algebraic-space]. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], $Z=Y\times_XU$ is an algebraic space and its projection $r:Z\to Y$ is surjective etale. Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $b:V\to Z$. The composition $p=rb:V\to Y$ is surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests]. Let $a:V\to U$ be the other projection composed with $b$. These are actual fibre-product projections, and $gp=ea$. In particular $a$ is a morphism of schemes; it need not be flat or of finite type.

source.place: Tag 02X2 (lemma-fibre-product-spaces); spaces-topologies.tex Tag 041F (lemma-etale), composition and base change of covers; compatible charts for Tag 07TZ(3).

proof.text: Apply the tensor-composition comparison of [lem-trf-space-chart-adjunction-tensor-realization] to $(g,p)$ and $(e,a)$. Since $gp=ea$, it gives $p^*g^*M\simeq a^*e^*M$. These are the specified canonical module functors, and etale $p^*$ and $e^*$ are restrictions by the same cited statement. For $N_U$ of step 1, the pullback comparison in [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] therefore gives $$p^*g^*M\simeq a^*(N_U)_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq(a^*N_U)_{\mathrm{et}}.$$ The last $a^*$ inside parentheses is ordinary Zariski tensor pullback. The comparison is the tensor associativity map: locally $c\otimes(d\otimes m)$ maps to $c\,p^\sharp(d)\otimes m$ for the first composition, and analogously for the second. No preservation of kernels by $g^*$ or $a^*$ is asserted.

By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], $a^*N_U$ is quasi-coherent; by [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type](3), it is of finite type. Its associated etale module is quasi-coherent by the equivalence in step 1 and is of finite type by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison]. Step 4 identifies it with $p^*g^*M$. Thus $g^*M$ has local quasi-coherent presentations and finite generating families on the surjective etale chart $p$. These are local properties by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and the stated finite-type definition: for any etale scheme chart $W\to Y$, the pullback $W\times_YV\to W$ is a surjective etale scheme cover by [lem-trf-space-representable-etale-scheme-tests], on which the presentations restrict. They therefore give the required local presentations on every slice. Consequently $g^*M$ is quasi-coherent and of finite type.

source.place: section-properties-modules, local properties and etale locality; modules.tex Tag 01BG (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent); descent.tex Tag 05VG (lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties); morphisms.tex Tag 056J(3).

proof.text: Now [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support] applies both to $M$ and to $g^*M$. By step 4 and the scheme support equality [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type](3), $$|p|^{-1}\operatorname{Supp}_Y(g^*M)=\operatorname{Supp}_V(a^*N_U)=|a|^{-1}\operatorname{Supp}_U(N_U)=|a|^{-1}|e|^{-1}\operatorname{Supp}_X(M)=|p|^{-1}|g|^{-1}\operatorname{Supp}_X(M).$$ The last equality follows from $gp=ea$ on field-valued representatives, using [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Since $p$ is surjective, every $y\in|Y|$ has a $v\in|V|$ above it, and membership of $y$ in the two subsets is equivalent to membership of $v$ in these equal preimages. This proves the claimed equality. Empty spaces and the zero module give empty sets in the same calculation.
